title: 1974 FIFA World Cup
prose:
The tenth FIFA World Cup was staged in West Germany from 13 June to 7 July 1974, gathering sixteen teams in a format unlike the modern knockout. The first round divided the field into four groups of four, with the top two from each advancing to a second round of two further groups of four. There were no knockout semi-finals: the winners of the two second-round groups met in the final, while the runners-up contested the third-place match. The tournament also introduced the current FIFA World Cup Trophy, brought in after Brazil permanently retained the previous Jules Rimet Trophy by winning in 1970.

The early rounds delivered one of the competition's most charged encounters. In a first-round group match in Hamburg, East Germany, making their first World Cup appearance, beat West Germany 1-0 in a politically loaded meeting. It was the only time the two German sides would ever face one another, yet West Germany recovered to advance and ultimately win the tournament. The Netherlands, inspired by Johan Cruyff, captivated audiences with their fluid 'Total Football,' while Poland emerged as a surprise force, propelled by the goals of Grzegorz Lato.

The final, played before 78,200 spectators at Munich's Olympiastadion on 7 July, opened with drama. Johan Neeskens converted a penalty in the second minute to put the Netherlands ahead, the first penalty ever awarded in a World Cup final. Paul Breitner equalised from a penalty of his own in the 25th minute, the second spot-kick of the match and one to each side, before Gerd Muller struck the winner in the 43rd minute. West Germany triumphed 2-1 to claim their second title, twenty years after their first in 1954.

The Netherlands finished as runners-up, while Poland defeated Brazil to take third place. Grzegorz Lato of Poland was the tournament's top scorer with seven goals. No official Golden Ball existed in 1974; FIFA's Best Young Player recognition went to Poland's Wladyslaw Zmuda. Across the matches, total attendance reached 1,865,753, averaging roughly 49,099 per game.
